name: How much does a typical room addition cost, and what’s a realistic budget range?

mainEntity.name: How much does a typical room addition cost, and what’s a realistic budget range?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Most room additions fall into a wide range because costs depend on size, level of finish, and complexity. Instead of chasing averages, build a realistic range for *your* scope and set aside contingency money.

Square‑foot “rules of thumb” can mislead; a small bathroom can be more expensive per square foot than a simple bedroom. Focus on total project cost and what you can comfortably afford.

Key factors:
- Size and type of space (bed, bath, family room, ADU)
- Structural work: foundation, beams, roof changes
- Utility upgrades: electrical panel, HVAC, plumbing runs
- Finish level: standard vs. custom cabinets, tile, windows

List your must‑have features and ask contractors for an itemized estimate with allowances. Build in 10–20% extra for surprises and upgrades, and prioritize function over high‑end finishes if budget is tight. Adjust scope (size, features) before construction starts, not after.
acceptedAnswer.description: Costs vary widely, but what matters most is building a realistic budget for your specific space, structure, and finish level. Get at least two itemized estimates, include a 10–20% contingency for surprises, and adjust size or finishes early so the total project cost stays within what you can comfortably afford.
